what_it_does: A Mixture-of-Experts model (MoE — a type of AI model that is divided into many 'specialist' sub-networks, of which only a small handful are activated for any given input) can have many more total parameters than a conventional model while using the same amount of computation per step. The flip side is that storing those parameters across thousands of machines is expensive, and if one machine crashes during training, you need to restore from a checkpoint — a saved snapshot of all parameters. Because most expert parameters exist even when they are not being used, checkpointing everything wastes enormous amounts of storage and time. MoC-System (Model-on-Checkpoint) takes advantage of the fact that in any single training step, only a small fraction of experts were actually updated. It therefore saves only those updated experts rather than the entire model, dramatically shrinking checkpoint size. It also overlaps the writing of checkpoint data with the normal forward-and-backward passes of training, hiding the checkpoint cost, and splits checkpoint shards across machines so no single machine is overwhelmed. The result is that fault recovery remains practical even when training runs on more than 10,000 machines simultaneously.
